newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hanbo Group faces parliamentary probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hanbo Group faces parliamentary probe.

text.p: South Korea's ruling party on Monday bowed to opposition demands and agreed to a parliamentary probe into the Hanbo Group whose steel unit has collapsed under a mountain of debt.
The New Korea Party agreed to the investigation on condition it did not hamper a separate probe by state prosecutors, a party statement said.
The ruling party accused the opposition of spreading "unfounded rumours" about the Hanbo Group and said the probe must involve the opposition as well as the ruling camp.

"Our party has firstly urged prosecutors to carry out a thorough government-level investigation in which we will cooperate, and secondly decided to open parliament as soon as possible to discuss any issues, including this matter," the statement said.
It quoted a party spokesman as saying the ruling camp also agreed to open a parliamentary probe.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics and the United Liberal Party said state prosecutors were not fit to examine the scandal because there were suspicions the government had supported loans to Hanbo despite its shaky status.
